question: What is the primary goal of inhalation therapy?

options.A: To deliver medication directly to the respiratory tract
options.B: To remove excess fluid directly from the pleural space
options.C: To bypass the digestive system completely for nutrition
options.D: To increase blood pressure through systemic absorption

explanation: Inhalation therapy deposits drugs straight into the airways and lungs for a localized effect. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why is inhalation therapy often preferred over oral medications for lung conditions?

options.A: It guarantees 100 percent absorption into the bloodstream
options.B: It works faster locally and reduces widespread side effects
options.C: It is completely free of any potential complications
options.D: It never requires patient coordination or special training

explanation: Targeting the lungs directly means smaller doses can treat the problem without affecting the rest of the body as heavily. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which part of the respiratory tract filters out large particles before they reach the lungs?
explanation: The nasal passages and upper airway warm, humidify, and filter incoming air, catching larger debris and particles. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h2)

question: What particle size is generally needed for medication to reach the deep lower airways and alveoli?
explanation: Fine particles measuring 1 to 5 micrometers are small enough to bypass the upper airway and settle deep in the bronchioles and alveoli. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which inhalation device requires the patient to take a fast, forceful breath to activate medication delivery?
explanation: Dry Powder Inhalers rely entirely on the patient's own inhalation effort to pull the powder out of the device and into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h3)

question: When is a nebulizer most commonly chosen over a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: When the patient needs a device that fits easily in a small shirt pocket
options.B: When treatment must be completed in less than five seconds
options.C: When the patient cannot coordinate deep breathing with a handheld inhaler
options.D: When the healthcare provider wants to avoid using any electricity or gas

explanation: Nebulizers produce a continuous mist over several minutes, making them great for young children, the elderly, or acutely breathless patients. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary condition treated using emergency inhaled bronchodilators?
explanation: Bronchodilators relax tightened airway muscles, making them the primary treatment for sudden breathing constriction or asthma attacks. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h4)

question: A patient with thick, sticky mucus blocking their airways is most likely to be prescribed which type of inhalable medication?
explanation: Mucolytics are specifically designed to break down and thin thick respiratory secretions so they can be cleared more easily. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the best body position for a patient receiving inhalation therapy?

options.A: Flat on the back with a low pillow
options.B: Lying flat on the left side
options.C: Pronated face down on the bed
options.D: Upright sitting or high Fowler's position

explanation: Sitting upright allows the diaphragm to move freely and promotes maximum lung expansion during medication delivery. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why must a nurse assess a patient's breathing technique and coordination before handing them an inhaler?

options.A: Assessment ensures the patient will never experience any drug side effects
options.B: All inhalation devices function identically regardless of the patient's skill
options.C: Patients are legally required to pass a written test before treatment
options.D: Different devices require specific breathing maneuvers for the drug to work

explanation: An MDI requires slow, deep breaths with a spacer, while a DPI requires a sharp inhalation, so matching technique is critical. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h5)

question: How long should a patient typically hold their breath after inhaling a dose of medication from an inhaler?
explanation: Holding the breath for about 10 seconds allows the tiny medication particles time to settle deep into the lung tissue instead of being exhaled right away. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h6)

question: What should the nurse instruct the patient to do immediately before actuating a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: Inhale as fast as possible through the nose
options.C: Exhale completely to empty the lungs
options.D: Take a quick swallow of cold water

explanation: Exhaling fully clears space in the lungs so the subsequent slow, deep inhalation can pull maximum medication into the airways. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which complication can occur if a patient fails to rinse their mouth after using an inhaled corticosteroid?

options.A: Sudden closure of the vocal cords

explanation: Residual steroid powder left in the oral cavity alters normal flora, frequently causing fungal overgrowth known as oral thrush. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why might a patient experience a fast heartbeat (tachycardia) and hand tremors after using a rescue inhaler?

options.A: The inhaler device was shaken upside down before use
options.B: The patient drank cold water right before taking the medication
options.C: The medication has a systemic stimulant effect on beta receptors
options.D: The patient held their breath for too long during administration

explanation: Rescue inhalers often contain beta-agonists which, when absorbed into the bloodstream, stimulate the heart and nervous system. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h7)

question: When a patient is prescribed both a bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid, which one should they generally use first?

options.A: Whichever medication is closer to hand
options.B: The corticosteroid to coat the throat
options.C: The bronchodilator to open the airways
options.D: Neither, they must be mixed together first

explanation: Using the bronchodilator first opens up the air passages, allowing the subsequent corticosteroid to penetrate much deeper into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h8)

question: A home care nurse is reviewing proper maintenance with a client who uses a metered-dose inhaler. What instruction should the nurse include?

options.A: Never clean the plastic mouthpiece housing to preserve the internal valve
options.B: Store the active inhaler device inside a humid bathroom cabinet
options.C: Check the built-in dose counter regularly to avoid running out of medication
options.D: Wash the pressurized metal canister inside a dishwasher once every week

explanation: Monitoring the dose counter ensures patients know when their medication is running low or empty before an emergency arises. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h8)
